newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone talks planned for Ivory Coast.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone talks planned for Ivory Coast.

text.p: A delegation from Sierra Leone's military rulers is due to meet a committee of West African foreign ministers in Ivory Coast on Thursday or Friday to discuss a standoff over their May 25 coup, officials said.
Officials in Ivory Coast were not immediately available for comment on the timing of the talks.

Sierra Leone's neighbours denounced the coup and opted in Guinea on June 26 for dialogue and economic sanctions to persuade the junta to restore ousted civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah to power. They retained the military option.
"The government is doing all in its power to ensure that the delegation leaves today for Abidjan despite flight difficulties," a senior foreign ministry official said.

A four-nation committee including regional power Nigeria and Ivory Coast, which brokered a truce between Kabbah's government and rebels last November, was to meet the junta and report to Nigeria's military leader, Sani Abacha, current chairman of the Economic Community of West African States.
Ghana and Guinea are also on the committee.

The junta's foreign minister, Paolo Bangura, heads its delegation. It includes Attorney General Manley Spaine and John Karefa Smart, leader of the second largest party in parliament after Kabbah's. The army and rebels, who rallied to the coup, will also be represented.
Kabbah came to power in 1996, defeating Karefa Smart in multi-party elections and ending four years of military rule.
Nigeria had troops in Sierra Leone before the coup under a peace deal. It has since reinforced. Ghana and Guinea also have troops there.
